meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

A 40-minute in-class draft and an essay written over a weekend are different conditions, Hale. People improve when they have time to revise. Turn both pages toward me, and you still haven't said whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
I'm writing that down: the checker is off the table. Now the version history, Hale. What does it show, and when?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to take the checker off the table and rely on the writing and the version history. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and a written promise that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal involved; that is not yet the fair outcome, because the private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 never came up, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You dropped the detector score and named the September 24 writing sample, which earned a little ground, but she never saw the pages or any version history times, so it could not move her further.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero unanswered, so it stayed her strongest point.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got near that night, since you gave no times from the version history, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after her first question, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put the version history on the table with its dates and times.
